chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Munzir ibn Yazeed, from Yunus ibn Zibyan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who fasts for the sake of Allah for a day in intense heat, so thirst hits him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, assigns a thousand angels to him, wiping his face and giving him glad tidings. Until when he breaks his fast, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "How aromatic is your fragrance and your spirit. My angels! Bear witness that I have forgiven him."'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting in intense heat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the virtue of enduring physical hardship in fasting, a concept central to Shia spiritual discipline. It illustrates the tangible divine reward through the intercession of a thousand angels and culminates in a direct divine declaration of forgiveness, witnessed by the celestial hosts. This emphasizes the intimate connection between bodily sacrifice and spiritual purification in Shia theology.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Munzir Bin Yazeed, from Yunus Bin Zibyan who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who Fasts for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for a day in intense heat, so thirst hits him, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Allocates a thousand Angels with him, wiping his face and giving him glad tidings until when he breaks fast, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Says: ‘How aromatic is your fragrance and your spirit. My Angels! Bear witness that I<sup>azwj</sup> have Forgiven him’.
en.sarwar: 17. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mundhir ibn Yazid from Yunus ibn Zabayan who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If one, for the sake of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, fasts on a very hot day, causing him to experience a great deal of thirst, Allah assigns a thousand angels for his safety who wipe his face until the time he discontinues his fast. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, then says, “How fine is your fragrance and spirit! O My angels, bear witness that I have granted him forgiveness.””’
